Hello, I'm so glad you're getting into blues! It's great music and there's lots of it.

To answer your main question briefly, check out this 1997 single from Johnny Lang. https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=3tigVYfHVmQ

That song 'Lie To Me' was huge on the radio when it was released, as part of a late 90's resurgence in the genre, along with other young artists like Kenny Wayne Shepherd.

Based on the artists you mentioned, you are definitely digging around in the roots of blues, which is the best place to start. I'll mention a few other artists that you should definitely listen to, assuming you haven't only because they weren't mentioned.

Robert Nighthawk - old style bluesman, known well among artists of his time.
Peter Green's Fleetwood Mac -- Peter Green was a top 5 blues player in his day, almost magically good at times.
Jimi Hendrix -- Start with the song 'Red House' and then just listen to the whole Jimi: Blues album.
Stevie Ray Vaughn (SRV) -- another all time great, had the 'Hendrix' style down pat, could also be considered progressive blues at times.
Taj Mahal -- multi talented artist with a specialty in blues, check out "Leavin' Trunk", and "Celebrated Walkin' Blues"
Ronnie Earl -- Catfish Blues (2000) https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=ohdD6R3GnkA -- instrumental

I've liked Chris Thomas King for a long time now. Delta Blues I think it's called. South Louisiana and up the Mississippi to Arkansas. A little tapping, a little slide, and bit of story telling. Though not as flashy as Stevie Ray or Kenny Wayne Shepherd, I connect more to the rhythm, am familiar with the lifestyle (grew up poor in Louisiana)... that's just me though.

CTK's Red Mud. https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=3NfKcuvO6VI

Don't get wrong, I like the more paced stuff too.

Tom Waits has more than few songs that fit the whole Gospel/blues genre. His work is genre all it's own but his railroad themes and gravel-chewed delivery puts him in my blues column.
